summary:
Israel's military launched an operation in the occupied West Bank on Friday, which it said would last several days and include searches and building demolitions. The operation follows an attack by gunmen that killed two soldiers days before Israeli elections on October 27, where security is a key focus. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed a major offensive, and the military said two attackers were also killed.

Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, southern Jordan, on Friday, killing seven people. Injury counts differ, with 34 wounded in one report and 40 in another. Authorities described the attack as a terrorist act motivated by extremist ideology, and Jordan's king vowed “the harshest retaliation”. A manhunt is under way.

Kenya's health ministry said on Friday that a 65-year-old woman, a close relative of the first patient, had died of Ebola, the country's second death. She developed symptoms while in quarantine, and the seven remaining patients are being treated at two isolation facilities. In Tibet, a magnitude-7 earthquake killed at least 16 people and injured 54, officials said, destroying hundreds of homes in the city of Nagqu.

headlines.title: Israel launches West Bank operation after two soldiers killed
headlines.summary: Israel's military began a several-day operation in the occupied West Bank on Friday, including searches and building demolitions. It followed a gunmen attack that killed two soldiers days before the October 27 Israeli elections.

headlines.title: Gunmen kill seven at church funeral in Jordan
headlines.summary: Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, southern Jordan, on Friday, killing seven people. The number wounded is given as 34 in one count and 40 in another, and a manhunt is under way.

headlines.title: Kenya reports second Ebola death, a close relative of first patient
headlines.summary: Kenya's health ministry said a 65-year-old woman, a close relative of the first patient, died after developing symptoms in quarantine. The remaining seven patients are being treated at two isolation facilities, and no new infections were reported.

headlines.title: Magnitude-7 earthquake in Tibet kills at least 16
headlines.summary: A magnitude-7 earthquake hit northern Tibet, killing at least 16 people, injuring 54 and destroying hundreds of homes in the city of Nagqu, officials said. Search and rescue efforts are under way after at least seven aftershocks were recorded.

headlines.title: Typhoon Champi kills one and injures hundreds in Taiwan
headlines.summary: Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, killing one person and uprooting trees, with injuries given as 350 in one count and over 500 in another. Much of Taiwan, including Taipei, stayed mostly closed with flights cancelled as the storm headed toward China.

headlines.title: France deploys 70,000 police as protests planned
headlines.summary: France is deploying about 70,000 police across the country on Saturday to prevent further civil unrest after some of the worst street violence in years. Authorities pledged to do everything in their power to prevent looting, violence and vandalism.

headlines.title: Macron calls Paris-area shooting a racist terrorist attack
headlines.summary: A gunman firing from a car killed one person and wounded five in the Paris suburbs on Friday, including a 12-year-old girl, though another count gives four wounded. President Emmanuel Macron called it a “racist terrorist attack”, and the suspect was arrested.
